reasons: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.

Root cause confirmed by source diff: introducing commit baad75cafa6b ("aacdec_usac: add support for parsing Mpsp212") added aacdec_usac_mps212.c/.h and parse_mps212(), which consume e->mps.otts_bands_phase (a raw 5-bit bitstream field, max 31) as an unclamped `end_band` array-bound parameter passed into ff_aac_ec_data_dec() for the IPD ("phase") data set, while the only validation present (mps_fr_nb_bands[freq_res], max 28) bounds a *different*, correctly-used `nb_bands` for the CLD/ICC data sets. The companion fix (ddcb9dd3b5d2, = post_benign) adds `if (otts_bands_phase > numBands) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;` (and the analogous check for bsResidualBands) directly in decode_usac_element_pair(), rejecting the malformed config before the bad value can ever reach parse_mps212().

No existing PoC/container-level reproducer was available, and hand-building a full valid USAC/xHE-AAC bitstream (AudioSpecificConfig + SBR header + arithmetic-coded core spectral data, all of which must be correctly parsed before parse_mps212 is ever reached in the real decode path) was infeasible relative to directly exercising the two functions the bug actually lives in. I therefore drove the real, unmodified vulnerable functions (via source #include of the untouched target .c file, not a rewritten copy) with a minimal, precisely bit-level-designed GetBitContext that reproduces exactly what the real bitstream fields would contain for this scenario. run_poc via the SAME run.sh/input on all three configured versions shows: (1) pre_intro accepts the same unchecked value at the config stage (ret=0) but the vulnerable sink is structurally absent (confirmed both by a failed compile and by grep); (2) post_intro accepts the same config and crashes deterministically under AddressSanitizer with a stack-buffer-overflow exactly where the root-cause description says the bound is missing; (3) post_benign rejects the same out-of-range config value before the sink is ever reached, and does not crash. A negative control with an in-bounds value (28) produces no crash on post_intro, isolating the defect to the out-of-range field rather than to the harness itself. The sanitizer fires as a stack WRITE overflow rather than literally as a "read," but per the ground rules a sanitizer report establishing the same regression under the same reproducer is accepted even when the precise sub-type label is imprecise; the underlying defect (missing bounds check on bsOttBandsPhase/bsResidualBands used as an array bound, exactly as described in meta.json's root_cause and findings) is unambiguously introduced by baad75cafa6b and fixed by the benign commit.

agent_oracle.description: No pre-existing PoC was available (source=no_poc). /poc/run.sh compiles and runs a harness that #includes the real, unmodified target file /work/libavcodec/aac/aacdec_usac.c (to reach its static functions) and calls the actual target functions decode_usac_element_pair() and parse_mps212() directly with a hand-crafted GetBitContext -- built this way because constructing a full container+ASC+SBR+arithmetic-coded-spectrum bitstream to reach parse_mps212 via the top-level decoder would exercise the exact same two functions but at far greater construction cost. Files: harness_config.c/harness_config_pre.c (stage 1: config parsing, compiles on all 3 revisions), harness_frame.c (stage 2: feeds a crafted per-frame MPS212 payload into parse_mps212(); only compiles where that function/struct exist), harness_frame_safe.c (negative control, in-bounds value). run.sh tries harness_frame.c first and falls back to harness_config_pre.c if it fails to build (expected pre-intro). Crafted bits (identical content across revisions): config stage sets bsFreqRes=1 (numBands=28 per Table 39 / mps_fr_nb_bands[]), bsPhaseCoding=1, bsOttBandsPhasePresent=1, bsOttBandsPhase=31 (5-bit max, 3 over the 28 limit), stereo_config_index=1; frame stage supplies a minimal MPS212 payload (CLD/ICC via data_mode=0 "default fill", then IPD via data_mode=3 -> ec_pair_dec with pcm_coding=0, dim=0, 31 one-bit Huffman-zero IPD symbols).
agent_oracle.target_evidence:
run_poc(post_intro) [commit baad75cafa6b]: exit=134, crashed=True. AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow, WRITE of size 2, in ec_pair_dec (aacdec_usac_mps212.c) <- ff_aac_ec_data_dec (aacdec_usac_mps212.c:646) <- parse_mps212 (aacdec_usac.c:1444) <- main (harness_frame.c:117). ASan's frame dump identifies the overflowed object as 'last_msb.i', declared `int16_t last_msb[MPS_MAX_PARAM_BANDS]` (28 entries, aacdec_usac_mps212.c:425); the overflow occurs at loop index 28 in `for (i=0;i<nb_bands;i++) last_msb[i]=last[i+start_band]+quant_offset;` where nb_bands == ec->mps.otts_bands_phase == 31, the unchecked bsOttBandsPhase value -- exactly 3 past the declared bound, matching meta.json's stated root cause (bsOttBandsPhase/bsResidualBands parsed via get_bits() and never range-checked against numBands before being used as an array bound).

run_poc(pre_intro) [commit 86977fdb6bb0]: exit=0, crashed=False. decode_usac_element_pair() accepts the same crafted bits (ret=0, otts_bands_phase=31 stored, no validation) -- identical unsafe field storage already exists pre-intro -- but harness_frame.c fails to even COMPILE against this revision ("unknown type name 'AACUsacMPSData'"), because aacdec_usac_mps212.c/.h and parse_mps212() (the vulnerable sink that uses otts_bands_phase as an array bound) do not exist at all pre-intro. This is confirmed independently by `grep -n parse_mps212` returning nothing pre-intro.

run_poc(post_benign) [fix ddcb9dd3b5d2 applied]: exit=0, crashed=False. decode_usac_element_pair() with the identical crafted bits now returns ret=-1094995529 (AVERROR_INVALIDDATA) because otts_bands_phase(31) > numBands(28); the harness correctly never proceeds to call parse_mps212 (mirroring the real decoder, where this negative return aborts config decode before any frame is ever processed). No crash.

Negative control (harness_frame_safe.c, otts_bands_phase=28, in-bounds) built and run directly against post_intro via docker_shell: parse_mps212 returns 0, no ASan report -- isolates the crash to the out-of-range value specifically, not to some unrelated harness defect.
